components.name: Blank Board
components.description: Blank circuit board
notes: Use 'Explicit' value for 'Dimension Mode' when placing a new board. The single control point places the top-left corner and 'Explicit Length' and 'Explicit Width' properties determine the dimensions
Set 'Underside Display' only if explicitly asked to. The values other than 'NONE' render the mirror image of the board in the provided direction with the offset controlled by 'Underside Offset'
Use this board as a base of PCB, eyelet and turret boards unless asked otherwise

components.name: Breadboard
components.description: Prototyping solderless breadboard
notes: The control point is the top-left corner of the body and 'Orientation' rotates the board around it. The body is 2.3in wide and 3.1in (Half) or 6.4in (Full) long

With 'Orientation' DEFAULT, terminal row n is n x 0.1in below the control point; columns a-e are 0.6-1.0in and f-j 1.3-1.7in to the right of it. Holes a-e of a row are connected, as are f-j; DIP ICs straddle the gap between e and f
Each side has two power rail columns connected along their full length: '+' at 0.2in and '-' at 0.3in on the left, '+' at 2.0in and '-' at 2.1in on the right. Rail holes come in groups of five

components.name: Eurorack Stripboard
components.description: David Haillant's eurorack format stripboard for prototyping and building simple modules

components.name: Eyelet Board
components.description: Perforated board with eyelets
notes: Use 'Explicit' value for 'Dimension Mode' when placing a new board. The single control point places the top-left corner and 'Explicit Length' and 'Explicit Width' properties determine the dimensions
Set 'Underside Display' only if explicitly asked to. The values other than 'NONE' render the mirror image of the board in the provided direction with the offset controlled by 'Underside Offset'
Use this type of board only when explicitly asked for a prefabricated grid eyelet board; most eyelet boards are built on blank boards
This board comes with pre-installed eyelets spaced apart equally
'Spacing' sets the center-to-center pitch of the eyelet grid; the first row and column of eyelet centers sit one 'Spacing' in from the top and left edges
Typically requires no additional eyelets or turrets

components.name: Marshall Style Perf Board
components.description: Perforated board as found on some Marshall and Trainwreck amps
notes: Use 'Explicit' value for 'Dimension Mode' when placing a new board. The single control point places the top-left corner and 'Explicit Length' and 'Explicit Width' properties determine the dimensions
Set 'Underside Display' only if explicitly asked to. The values other than 'NONE' render the mirror image of the board in the provided direction with the offset controlled by 'Underside Offset'
Use this type of board only when explicitly asked to
This board comes with pre-drilled holes spaced apart equally
'Spacing' sets the center-to-center pitch of the hole grid; the first row and column of hole centers sit one 'Spacing' in from the top and left edges
There are no conductive surfaces on this board; place eyelets or turrets exactly on the holes to create connection points

components.name: P-0+o (Proto) Board
components.description: A prototyping board for modular synths, central bus with V+ GND and V-
notes: The control point is the top-left corner of the 2in x 4in body and 'Orientation' rotates the board around it

With 'Orientation' DEFAULT, pad row n (1-33) is (0.4 + n x 0.1)in below the control point. Each row is split into separately connected groups, labeled by column: 1-2, 3-5, 6-8, 9-11, 12-14 and 15-16, at 0.1-0.2, 0.4-0.6, 0.7-0.9, 1.2-1.4, 1.5-1.7 and 1.8-1.9in to the right of it

components.name: Perf Board w/ Pads
components.description: Perforated board with solder pads
notes: Use 'Explicit' value for 'Dimension Mode' when placing a new board. The single control point places the top-left corner and 'Explicit Length' and 'Explicit Width' properties determine the dimensions
Set 'Underside Display' only if explicitly asked to. The values other than 'NONE' render the mirror image of the board in the provided direction with the offset controlled by 'Underside Offset'
This board comes with drilled copper pads spaced apart equally
'Spacing' sets the center-to-center pitch of the pad grid; the first row and column of pad centers sit one 'Spacing' in from the top and left edges

components.name: Proto Board 780 Holes
components.description: Prototyping board similar to Radio Shack 276-168B or MPJA 33304

components.name: Tag Strip
components.description: Row of terminals for point-to-point construction
notes: Each terminal is an independent connection point; the mounting lugs are not connection points

components.name: Terminal Strip
components.description: Row of terminals for point-to-point construction
notes: Each terminal is one node made of its A and B holes, plus C when 'Center Terminal' is on; separate terminals are not connected

components.name: TriPad Board
components.description: Perforated FR4 board with copper strips connecting 3 holes in a row (aka TriPad Board)
notes: Use 'Explicit' value for 'Dimension Mode' when placing a new board. The single control point places the top-left corner and 'Explicit Length' and 'Explicit Width' properties determine the dimensions
Set 'Underside Display' only if explicitly asked to. The values other than 'NONE' render the mirror image of the board in the provided direction with the offset controlled by 'Underside Offset'
Hole centers follow 'Spacing' like Perf Board: the first row and column sit one 'Spacing' in from the top and left edges
Copper strips run along 'Orientation' and join 'Holes Per Strip' consecutive holes, counted from the left edge (HORIZONTAL) or top edge (VERTICAL); neighbouring strips are not connected

components.name: Vero Board
components.description: Perforated FR4 board with copper strips connecting all holes in a row
notes: Use 'Explicit' value for 'Dimension Mode' when placing a new board. The single control point places the top-left corner and 'Explicit Length' and 'Explicit Width' properties determine the dimensions
Set 'Underside Display' only if explicitly asked to. The values other than 'NONE' render the mirror image of the board in the provided direction with the offset controlled by 'Underside Offset'
Hole centers follow 'Spacing' like Perf Board: the first row and column sit one 'Spacing' in from the top and left edges
With 'Orientation' HORIZONTAL every row of holes is one continuous copper strip, with VERTICAL every column; break a strip with a 'Trace Cut'

components.name: Copper Trace
components.description: Straight copper trace
notes: Use for copper on PCB layouts; for a wire link use Jumper or Hookup Wire
A single straight segment on the copper side chosen by 'Layer'; chain segments end to end for bends, or use Curved Trace
The whole length is copper: any terminal or copper on the same layer that it touches or crosses is connected, not just its ends, so traces of different nets must not cross

components.name: Curved Trace
components.description: Curved copper trace
notes: Use for a curved copper trace on a PCB layout; for a straight one use Copper Trace
The whole length is copper: any terminal or copper on the same layer that it touches or crosses is connected, not just its ends, so traces of different nets must not cross
Only the first and last control points are the trace ends; the points between them are curve handles the trace does not necessarily pass through

components.name: Cut Line
components.description: Cut line

components.name: Dot
components.description: Connector dot
notes: A junction marker for schematics and wiring diagrams; it is drawing only and connects nothing, since ends that meet at the same point are already connected. For a pad on a board use Solder Pad

components.name: Eyelet
components.description: Eyelet or turret terminal
notes: Every lead, wire or terminal end placed inside its 'Size' circle is connected to it, so bring all the ends that share a node to the same eyelet

components.name: Ground Fill
components.description: Polygonal ground fill area

components.name: Hookup Wire
components.description: Insulated flexible wire, straight or curved
notes: Use for insulated wiring on or off the board, such as runs to pots, jacks and switches; for a bare link between two holes use Jumper, and for each conductor of a twisted pair in a circuit that must be analyzable use one Hookup Wire, since Twisted Leads is a single conductor drawn for looks
Only the first and last control points are wire ends; the points between them are curve handles the wire does not necessarily pass through

components.name: Jumper
components.description: Straight bare wire link between two holes
notes: Use for a bare-wire link between two holes, typically on perf and strip boards; for insulated or off-board wiring use Hookup Wire, and for copper on a PCB use Copper Trace

components.name: Multimeter Probe
components.description: Multimeter Probe

components.name: PCB Terminal Block
components.description: Horizontal PCB terminal block with configurable pitch

components.name: Right Angle Wire
components.description: Wire that runs horizontally and vertically and turns at right angles

components.name: Solder Lug
components.description: Locking terminal lug commonly used for chassis ground connections

components.name: Solder Pad
components.description: Copper solder pad, round or square
notes: Use on Blank Board and PCB layouts; Perf Board, Vero Board, TriPad Board and the proto boards already have their own pads

components.name: Trace Cut
components.description: Designates the place where a trace on the vero board needs to be cut
notes: Place the control point on a hole centre. By default the copper around that hole is removed, cutting the strip there and leaving the hole itself connected to nothing

With 'Cut Between Holes' the cut runs between that hole and the one to its left ('Cut Orientation' VERTICAL) or above it (HORIZONTAL), and both holes stay on their part of the strip. 'Cut Orientation' is the direction of the cut, so a Vero Board with HORIZONTAL strips needs VERTICAL cuts

components.name: Turret Lug
components.description: Turret terminal lug
notes: Every lead, wire or terminal end placed inside its 'Size' circle is connected to it, so bring all the ends that share a node to the same turret

components.name: Twisted Leads
components.description: A pair of flexible leads twisted tightly together
notes: Electrically a single conductor between its two ends, exactly like Hookup Wire, even though two twisted leads are drawn; use it only for the look of a twisted pair, and where the circuit must be electrically correct and analyzable, draw each conductor as its own Hookup Wire or Right Angle Wire instead
The points between the first and last are curve handles the leads do not necessarily pass through

components.name: 9V Battery Snap
notes: The first control point is the + terminal, at the middle of the snap's flat end where the leads come out; the - terminal is 0.1in below it in DEFAULT 'Orientation', the body extends to the right and the other orientations rotate this around the + terminal

components.name: Chassis Panel
components.description: One side of a chassis, with or withouth rounded edges
notes: Each instance is one side of the chassis: an exploded view of a whole chassis takes five panels, while the top, front and back alone take three, which is typical for pedals and amplifiers. The top panel goes in the centre with the front panel against its upper edge and the back panel against its lower edge; in the five-panel view the left side panel goes against its left edge and the right side panel against its right edge
The panel is not conductive in the netlist: jacks, pots and lugs drawn on it are not joined through it, so chassis ground points must be connected explicitly

components.name: Cliff 1/4" Jack
components.description: Cliff-style closed panel mount 1/4" phono jack
notes: The first control point is a corner lug; with 'Orientation' DEFAULT the lugs sit on the corners of a 0.6in square to the right of and below it, Tip Switch and Tip down the left side and Sleeve Switch and Sleeve down the right, and STEREO adds Ring Switch and Ring midway along the top and bottom edges. The body is centred on the square with its threaded nose pointing right, and the other orientations rotate all of this clockwise around the first lug

components.name: Cliff 1/8" Jack
components.description: Cliff-style closed 1/8" phono jack

components.name: Closed 1/4" Jack
components.description: Enclosed panel mount 1/4" phono jack
notes: The first control point is the Tip lug; with 'Orientation' DEFAULT the Sleeve lug is 0.8in to the right of it, near the far end of the body, and for STEREO the Ring lug is 0.2in below the Tip lug. The body runs to the right from the Tip lug with the threaded bushing beyond it, and the other orientations rotate all of this around the Tip lug

components.name: DIP Switch
components.description: Dual-in-line package switch

components.name: Drill Hole
components.description: Drill hole marker for PCB, chassis or faceplate

components.name: Elliptical Cutout
components.description: Elliptical chassis cutout

components.name: Fuse Holder (Panel)
components.description: Panel mounted fuse holder
notes: The two control points are the lugs, 0.2in apart: the second is below the first with 'Orientation' VERTICAL and to its right with HORIZONTAL, and the round body is centred between them

components.name: IEC Socket
components.description: Panel mounted IEC power socket
notes: The Earth lug is centred on the chamfered side of the outline; with 'Orientation' DEFAULT the Line lug sits 0.3in to its left and the Neutral lug 0.3in to its right, both 0.2in below it, and the mounting holes are 40mm apart on the line halfway between. The other orientations rotate this around the Earth lug

components.name: Mini Relay
components.description: Miniature PCB mount relay, like Omron G5V-1 or G5V-2
notes: The first control point is the anchor; with 'Orientation' DEFAULT the first column of pins runs down from it, the second column sits to the right and the indent is at the anchor's end. The other orientations rotate this around the anchor

Pin offsets down each column from the anchor: Miniature DPDT 0, 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7in, SPDT 0, 0.5 and 0.7in, columns 0.3in apart; Ultra_miniature DPDT 0, 0.2, 0.3 and 0.4in, SPDT 0, 0.3 and 0.4in, columns 0.2in apart

components.name: Mini Toggle Switch
components.description: Panel mounted mini toggle switch
notes: The first control point is the anchor; with 'Orientation' VERTICAL each pole is a column of three lugs (two for SPST) running down from it 'Spacing' apart, and further poles sit 'Spacing' apart to the right. HORIZONTAL turns this 90 degrees counterclockwise around the anchor, so each pole runs to the right and further poles stack upward

components.name: Neutrik 1/4" Jack
components.description: 1/4" mono/stereo phono jack based on Neutrik NMJx series, PCB or Panel-mount

components.name: Open 1/4" Jack
components.description: Switchcraft-style open panel mount 1/4" phono jack, stereo and mono
notes: The first control point is the Tip lug; with 'Angle' 0 the jack's centre is 0.5in below it and the other lugs sit around that centre: Sleeve to the upper right and, for STEREO, Ring to the lower right; for SWITCHED, Sleeve to the lower left and Shunt to the upper left. 'Angle' rotates the whole jack clockwise around the Tip lug, in degrees

components.name: Open 1/8" Jack
components.description: Switchcraft-style open panel mount 1/8" phono jack, stereo and mono

components.name: Pilot Lamp Holder
components.description: Fender-style pilot bulb holder for T2 and T-3 ¼ miniature bayonet lamps
notes: The first control point is the upper hole of the lug for the bulb's centre contact; with 'Angle' 0 its other hole, pin 3, is 0.1in below it and the lamp centre 0.4in below it. Pins 2 and 4 are the matching holes of the shell lug, which is the same lug turned 53 degrees clockwise around the lamp centre. 'Angle' rotates the holder clockwise around the first pin, in degrees. The netlist does not join the two holes of a lug, so each is a terminal of its own

components.name: Pin Header
components.description: PCB mount male pin header with editable number or pins and pin spacing
notes: The first control point is pin 1; with 'Orientation' DEFAULT 'Columns' sets how many pins run straight down from it and 'Rows' how many such lines sit side by side to the right, all 'Spacing' apart, so the default 2 'Rows' x 5 'Columns' is two vertical lines of five pins. The other orientations rotate this around pin 1

Pins are numbered down the first line and then down the next, so in the default header pin 6 is beside pin 1; 'Node Names' is a comma-separated list in that order, and a blank entry keeps the pin's number

components.name: Plastic DC Jack
components.description: Panel mount plastic DC jack
notes: The Switch lug is 0.1in to the right of and 0.1in below the Sleeve lug, and the Center lug 0.1in to the left of and 0.2in below it; the round body is centred 0.1in below the Sleeve lug

components.name: Polygonal Cutout
components.description: Polygonal chassis cutout

components.name: RCA Jack
components.description: Panel mount RCA phono jack socket
notes: The first control point is the Tip contact at the centre of the jack; the Sleeve lug is 0.5in below it in DEFAULT 'Orientation', and the other orientations rotate it around the centre

components.name: Rectangular Cutout
components.description: Rectangular chassis cutout, with or without rounded edges

components.name: Rotary Selector Switch
components.description: Single pole rotary switch, typically used for impedance selector
notes: The first control point is the Common lug and the centre of the switch is 20mm above it in DEFAULT 'Orientation'; the position lugs 1, 2, ... follow in 45 degree steps counterclockwise around that centre, so lug 1 is to the lower right. The other orientations rotate everything around the Common lug

components.name: Rotary Switch (Open)
components.description: Open rotary switch in several different switching configurations

components.name: Rotary Switch (Sealed)
components.description: Sealed plastic rotary switch in several different switching configurations

components.name: Slide Switch
components.description: Panel mounted slide switch

components.name: Tactile Micro-Switch
components.description: 4-pin tactile momentary switch

components.name: Thonk 3.5mm Jack
components.description: Thonkiconn style 3.5mm jack

components.name: Freeway 3X3-03 Switch
components.description: Freeway 3X3-03 (Standard) Toggle Switch
notes: The first control point is pad CA at the top of the board. With 'Orientation' DEFAULT, CB is 6mm to its right, the B pads run down a column 12mm to its right and the A pads up a column 6mm to its left, 4.5mm apart from 2mm to 24.5mm below CA, and GND is 27mm below CA and 3mm to the right. The other orientations rotate this clockwise around CA

components.name: Freeway 3X3-05 (Ultra) Switch
components.description: Freeway 3X3-05 (Ultra) Toggle Switch
notes: The first control point is pad 1B, the pad just left of the top of the round switch. The 28 pads sit on a circle of 15.3mm radius around the switch centre, which is 15.2mm below and 1.7mm right of 1B, and continue counterclockwise from it, so the first 14 (the B pads) form the left half and the rest (the A pads) the right half. 'Orientation' rotates the switch clockwise around 1B

components.name: Freeway Blade
components.description: Several variations of Freeway Blade switches
notes: The first control point is the first terminal; with 'Angle' 0 the terminals run up from it in a straight line 0.15in apart. 'Angle' rotates the switch clockwise in degrees

components.name: Humbucker Pickup
components.description: Double-coil humbucker guitar pickup (PAF, Mini Humbuckers, Filtertrons)
notes: With 'Orientation' DEFAULT the coils lie horizontally, the pickup's length running left to right; the other orientations rotate the pickup clockwise

The four control points run down the top-right edge of the pickup 0.1in apart in 'Orientation' DEFAULT, starting at the first one, and turn with the pickup, so they stay at the same corner of the body in every orientation

The wiring analysis takes the coils as in phase when the North coil has its Start and the South coil its Finish on the side of the output jack's Tip: the series humbucker takes North Start to hot, joins North Finish to South Finish and takes South Start to ground; in parallel, North Start and South Finish go to hot and North Finish and South Start to ground

components.name: Jazz Bass Pickup
components.description: Single coil pickup for Jazz Bass and similar guitars
notes: With 'Orientation' DEFAULT the coils lie horizontally, the pickup's length running left to right; the other orientations rotate the pickup clockwise

Set 'Coil(s)' to North for a regular single coil and South for a reverse-wound, reverse-polarity (RWRP) one; Humbucking gives the two coils of a four-conductor humbucker, and the Stacked values a stacked humbucker with two leads, which the wiring analysis takes as hum-cancelling on its own

The wiring analysis takes coils as in phase when they all run the same way between the output jack's Tip and Sleeve: a single coil, North or South, runs from Start at the Tip side to Finish at the Sleeve side, and a North and a South coil in phase cancel hum. With 'Coil(s)' Humbucking the South coil runs the other way, Finish at the Tip side, so the series humbucker takes North Start to hot, joins North Finish to South Finish and takes South Start to ground

The four control points run down the top-right edge of the pickup 0.1in apart in 'Orientation' DEFAULT, starting at the first one, and turn with the pickup, so they stay at the same corner of the body in every orientation; as a single coil it uses only the middle two as terminals

components.name: LP Toggle Switch
components.description: Les Paul style 3 position toggle switch
notes: Drawn from the bottom, where the solder lugs are. The first control point is the anchor at the top of the switch, not a switched terminal; with 'Orientation' DEFAULT the terminals sit in a row 1.3in below it, centred under it, 0.2in apart, or 0.1in apart with a gap in the middle when 'Middle Terminals' is Disconnected

components.name: Lever Switch
components.description: Strat-style lever switch
notes: The first control point is the first terminal; with 'Angle' 0 the terminals run down from it 0.1in apart (0.15in for DP3T_5pos_Import and DP3T_5pos_2502N), every second one offset 0.1in to the right on the zig-zag types. 'Angle' rotates the switch clockwise in degrees

components.name: S1 Switch
components.description: Fender S1 4 pole pushbutton switch
notes: The first control point is the anchor, not a terminal, 0.05in below the centre of the 1in disc. The twelve lugs sit in four groups of three on a 4.5mm grid around the disc centre: with 'Orientation' DEFAULT lugs 2-4 run left to right 9mm above the centre, 5-7 top to bottom 9mm right of it, 8-10 left to right 9mm below it and 11-13 top to bottom 9mm left of it; the other orientations rotate this clockwise around the anchor
Give the switch the same 'Orientation' as the panel potentiometer it is mounted on; the switching is not symmetric under rotation, and DEFAULT matches the pot's DEFAULT

components.name: Schaller Megaswitch

Type M has two columns of twelve 0.1in apart, about 2.6mm between columns: A to L run up from the first point, M to X come back down the column to its right, so X sits beside A. 'Angle' rotates the switch clockwise in degrees

components.name: Auto-Wrap Label

components.name: Mini Signal Transformer
components.description: Miniature PCB-mount signal transformer with EI core
notes: The first control point is the top primary pin; with 'Orientation' DEFAULT the primary pins run down from it and the secondary pins form a matching column 'Winding Spacing' to the right. Each winding spans 2 x 'Lead Spacing', with a centre tap pin midway when 'Primary CT' or 'Secondary CT' is set and only its two ends otherwise. Pins are numbered down the primary, then down the secondary, and the other orientations rotate this around the first pin

components.name: Multi-Section Capacitor
components.description: Multi-section vertically mounted electrolytic capacitor, similar to JJ, CE and others
notes: Each entry in 'Value' is one section; '+1', '+2', ... are the positive lugs of the sections in the order of the entries, and all sections share the '-' lug

The '-' lug is the anchor and the can is centred below it in DEFAULT 'Orientation'. With one section the '+' lug is 0.4 x 'Diameter' straight below the anchor; with two the '+' lugs sit 0.3 x 'Diameter' below it, one to the right and one to the left; with three or more all lugs lie evenly spaced clockwise from the anchor on a circle of 0.6 x 'Diameter' whose top is the anchor. The other orientations rotate this around the anchor

components.name: Potentiometer
components.description: Metal body panel mount potentiometer with solder lugs or PCB terminals (Alpha, CTS, Bourns)
notes: Leave 'View' at its default, ShaftDown, unless asked otherwise: the pot is seen from the back, and with 'Orientation' DEFAULT its lugs face down
The first control point is the anchor; with 'Orientation' DEFAULT the other two lugs run to the right of it 'Spacing' apart, and the other orientations rotate this around the anchor
Orient the pot so its lugs face the rest of the circuit: they face down in DEFAULT, left in _90, up in _180 and right in _270

Unless told otherwise, use one of two standard sizes, picked by the type of circuit and the space available: the 25mm pot, which the defaults already describe ('Diameter' 1in, 'Spacing' 0.3in), or the 16mm pot ('Diameter' 16mm, 'Spacing' 0.2in)

components.name: Transistor (TO-1)
components.description: Transistor with small metal body
notes: The first control point is the anchor; with 'Orientation' DEFAULT the third pin is 2 x 'Pin spacing' below it and the middle pin 'Pin spacing' below and 'Pin spacing' to the left, a triangle under the round can. 'Folded' puts the three pins in a straight line down from the anchor and lays the body flat on the right of them. The other orientations rotate this around the anchor
On a 0.1in grid board the default 0.05in 'Pin spacing' puts the middle pin between holes: set 'Pin spacing' to 0.1in to land all three pins on holes

components.name: Transistor (TO-220)
components.description: Transistors with metal tab for heat sink mounting
notes: The first control point is the anchor; with 'Orientation' DEFAULT the three pins run straight down from it 0.1in apart, and the other orientations rotate this around the anchor

Seen from above, the metal tab is on the right of the pin row in DEFAULT orientation and the printed front faces left; 'Folded' lays the body flat on the right of the pin row, 'Lead Length' away from it, with the tab and its mounting hole at the far end
'Pinout' values list the pins as a datasheet does, facing the printed front with the legs down, left to right; pick the value that matches the part's datasheet as written

components.name: Transistor (TO-92)
components.description: Transistor with small plastic or epoxy body
notes: The first control point is the anchor; with 'Orientation' DEFAULT the three pins run straight down from it 'Pin spacing' apart, and the other orientations rotate this around the anchor
Seen from above, the flat face is on the left of the pin row in DEFAULT orientation; 'Folded' lays the body flat on the right of the pin row instead
'Pinout' values list the pins as a datasheet does, facing the flat side with the legs down, left to right; pick the value that matches the part's datasheet as written

On a 0.1in grid board the default 0.05in 'Pin spacing' puts the middle pin between holes: set 'Pin spacing' to 0.1in, or use two or three jumpers acting as flexible leads and connecting TO-92 terminals to the holes on the board
